audit_of.title: SYNTHETIC TEMPLATE: replace every value in this file. A reminder-letter trial for dental check-ups
audit_of.source: Who published it: journal, organisation or vendor
audit_of.locator: The file name or address the audit was made from

claim.quote: Reminder letters increased attendance by a quarter.

supporting_result.quote: Attended within 3 months: 150 of 400 (37.5%) with a letter, 120 of 400 (30.0%) without.

design.ceiling: A randomised trial can show that the letter caused a difference in the people analysed, if allocation was concealed and follow-up was near complete. It cannot show the same effect in other clinics or over longer periods.

outcomes.name: Attended a check-up within 3 months
outcomes.definition: A check-up recorded in the clinic system within 90 days of randomisation

outcomes.name: Days from randomisation to check-up
outcomes.definition: Among those who attended, days between randomisation and the check-up

reporting.text: Registered before the first participant was enrolled; the registered primary outcome matches the one reported.
Computer-generated list held by a statistician outside the clinic.
Staff recording attendance did not know the allocation; participants could not be blinded.
Everyone with a clinic record at 3 months, in the group they were randomised to.
A regional health board grant; the funder had no role in the analysis.
All authors work at the clinic network that ran the trial.
